items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 7.2.2 at source lines 265-269, and both of the author's proofs are retained (source lines 271-313). The hard step in the first proof is a dependent-path computation: for a reflexive mere relation R implying identity one must read ap_{f(x)}(p) as a dependent path in the family R(x,x) -> (x = x), convert it with the arrow-type dependent path lemma into trans_p(f(x,x,r)) = f(x,x,trans_p r) (source lines 289-291), then use that R(x,x) is a mere proposition to collapse trans_p r to r and cancel to obtain p = refl_x (lines 293-296). The second proof is a different route that needs the total-space criterion for equivalences and the sigma path characterization to show Sm{y:X} R(x,y) contractible with centre (x, rho(x)) (lines 300-312). Neither step is a routine rewrite, and the statement alone supplies neither the transport bookkeeping nor the contractibility witness.
